learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how 'Culture' acts as our software for living, and how 'Socialisation' programs us from a biological baby into a social human being!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Culture is a way of life shared by members of a society. It includes Material culture (tools, buildings, clothes) and Non-material culture (beliefs, values, language). It is learned, not biologically inherited.
Culture has three main dimensions: Cognitive (how we process information and knowledge), Normative (rules of conduct and values), and Material (tangible objects and technology).
Ethnocentrism is the habit of judging other cultures by the standards of your own, often believing yours is superior. Cosmopolitanism is the opposite—respecting and valuing cultural differences.

Socialisation is a lifelong process by which individuals learn the norms, values, and behavior appropriate for their society. Primary socialisation happens in infancy (family), while secondary socialisation happens later (school, peers).
These are the groups that teach us how to be social. The main agencies are the Family (most important), Peer Groups (friends), Schools, and Mass Media (TV, internet).

fun_activity.title: 👽 The Alien Observer
fun_activity.instructions: Pretend you are an alien who just landed on Earth. Describe the 'cultural ritual' of blowing out candles on a birthday cake to your home planet. It sounds completely bizarre when you look at it objectively!

exam_tips: 📌 Distinguish between Material Culture (things you can touch) and Non-material Culture (ideas, values).
📌 Ethnocentrism is a very frequent exam question. Give the example of colonial rulers viewing indigenous cultures as 'backward'.
📌 Remember that socialisation is a *lifelong* process—it doesn't stop when you become an adult!
quick_recap: ⭐ Culture is dynamic; it constantly changes and adapts over time.
⭐ A 'Subculture' is a smaller cultural group within a larger society (e.g., bikers, gamers).
⭐ Family is the primary agency of socialisation, laying the foundation for a child's personality.
